latest_census.notes: 2021 Census of Population and Housing (10 August 2021). Religion: asked, voluntary, 'not stated' is a category. Ethnicity: no ethnicity question; the census asks ancestry (up to two responses per person, so not a partition) and, separately, Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander status (single response, a partition). Language: 'language used at home' (2016 wording 'language spoken at home'), single response, a partition. All are published in the General Community Profile at every ASGS level (STE, SA1-SA4, LGA, POA, ...): G07 Indigenous status by age by sex, G08 Ancestry by country of birth of parents, G13 Language used at home by proficiency in spoken English by sex, G14 Religious affiliation by sex. The 2026 Census was held on 11 August 2026 (recalled); first results are not due until mid-2027, so 2021 remains the latest with data.

already_in_map: Religion at 9 states and 547 LGAs from ABS Data API dataflow C21_G14_LGA (SOURCES.md 'Australia: a table that was there, and four religions that were not'). The adapter also fetches C21_G08_LGA ancestry and by design keeps it as a separate multi-response 'ancestry' field rather than 'ethnicity' (abs.py docstring: 'Australia has no ethnicity question ... the app keeps those as distinct fields rather than folding them into an ethnicity bucket'), so the packet's ethnicity=0 is a deliberate withhold, not a missing source. Language is a genuine gap: the adapter does not fetch G13.

summary: Australia's 2021 census asks religion, ancestry (multi-response, deliberately kept out of the map's ethnicity field), Indigenous status and language used at home, and publishes all of them for every LGA and state through the same ABS Data API the repo already reads for religion. Language is the real gap and is one more dataflow (GCP table G13, a clean single-response partition) in the existing adapter. Nothing is missing at the source; the 2026 Census was taken in August 2026 with results due 2027.
